options: The pilot must not fly if their ability is impaired or if they exceed specific blood-alcohol limits
The pilot may fly as long as they feel capable
The pilot may drink up to 2 units of alcohol 4 hours before flight
The pilot must wait 2 hours after consuming any alcohol

bank.question: According to the Standardised European Rules of the Air (SERA), what is the definition of 'Night'?
bank.explanation: SERA defines night in the UK as the period from the end of evening civil twilight until the beginning of morning civil twilight
options: From the end of evening civil twilight until the beginning of morning civil twilight
30 Minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
From 20:00 to 06:00 UTC regardless of light conditions

bank.question: The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has the power to issue a 'Restriction of Flying' (SI) for specific events like airshows
bank.explanation: Article 239 of the UK Air Navigation Order allows the CAA to restrict flying in specified airspace for reasons of public interest, safety, or security

bank.question: What is the minimum height an aircraft may fly over the congested area of a city, town, or settlement?
bank.explanation: An aircraft must not be flown over the congested area of a city, town, or settlement below a height of 1,000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600m

bank.question: How is 'Total Flight Time' recorded in a pilot's logbook defined?
bank.explanation: The 'Total Flight Time' is defined as the time from when the aircraft first moves for the purpose of taking off until it finally comes to rest at the end of the flight
options: From the moment the engine starts to the moment it stops
From the moment the wheels leave the ground to the moment they touch down
From the moment the aircraft first moves under its own power for the purpose of taking off until it comes to rest
The time spent in the air only

bank.question: Who is primarily responsible for ensuring an aircraft is airworthy and that all required documents are on board before a flight?
bank.explanation: The commander of an aircraft must ensure a 'fit-to-fly' self-assessment is made and that all required documents and fuel for the intended flight are on board

bank.question: A black letter 'C' on a yellow background in the signal square indicates that the aerodrome is currently closed
bank.explanation: A black letter 'C' on a vertical yellow background indicates the location of the Air Traffic Services Reporting Office (Reporting Point/Control Office)

bank.question: In Class D airspace, between which types of flight does Air Traffic Control provide separation?
bank.explanation: In Class D airspace, ATC provides separation between IFR/IFR flights, but VFR flights are responsible for their own separation from other VFR and IFR traffic (with traffic information provided)
options: ATC is not responsible for separation in Class D

bank.question: Which organisation is responsible for the administration of most amateur-built aircraft 'Permits to Fly' in the UK?
bank.explanation: The LAA (Light Aircraft Association) is the primary body delegated by the CAA to oversee the airworthiness of experimental and amateur-built aircraft under the Permit to Fly system

bank.question: Which international convention led to the establishment of ICAO?
bank.explanation: The Chicago Convention (1944) established the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the fundamental principles of international air law

bank.question: An aircraft taxiing on the maneuvering area of an aerodrome must give way to vehicles towing aircraft
bank.explanation: SERA states that if two aircraft are approaching head-on, both must alter course to the right. Rules of the air prioritize surface craft; aircraft must give way to them

bank.question: What is the definition of an Air Traffic Control Clearance?
bank.explanation: An Air Traffic Control Clearance is only valid for the specific portion of the flight or specific instructions provided and does not relieve the pilot of the responsibility to avoid collisions
options: Absolute right of way over all other aircraft
Permission to disregard the Rules of the Air
Authorization for an aircraft to proceed under conditions specified by an ATC unit
A guarantee that no other aircraft are in the immediate vicinity

bank.question: What is the internationally recognised visual signal used by ground personnel to warn an aircraft that it is flying in the vicinity of a restricted, prohibited, or danger area?
bank.explanation: White strobes or flashes are the standard visual signal from the ground to alert an aircraft that it is flying within or about to enter restricted, prohibited, or danger areas
options: Fire a green signal flare from the ground
Direct a series of white flashes at the aircraft from a signal lamp
A ground technician waves a large red flag side-to-side
The aerodrome will switch on its runway edge lights to full intensity

bank.question: When flying in the aerodrome circuit below the transition altitude, what pressure setting should be set on the altimeter?
bank.explanation: The altimeter should be set to the Aerodrome QNH to indicate the aircraft's altitude above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) while in the circuit

bank.question: The upper vertical limit of an Aerodrome Traffic Zone (ATZ) is 3,000ft Above Aerodrome Level (AAL)
bank.explanation: The ATZ usually extends from the surface to 2,000ft Above Aerodrome Level (AAL)

bank.question: What does a series of red flashes from Aerodrome Control indicate to an aircraft in the air?
bank.explanation: A series of red flashes from Aerodrome Control to an aircraft in the air means the aerodrome is unsafe and the pilot should not land
options: Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the apron

bank.question: When one aircraft is overtaking another, which aircraft has the right of way?
bank.explanation: Under the 'Rule of the Air' regarding right of way, the aircraft being overtaken (the slower one) has the right of way, and the overtaking aircraft must keep clear
options: Whichever aircraft is to the right of the other
The faster aircraft, as it can clear the hazard more quickly

bank.question: When two aircraft are approaching head-on and there is a danger of collision, what action should be taken by both pilots?
bank.explanation: When two aircraft are approaching head-on, or approximately so, both must alter their course to the right
options: Both aircraft shall alter course to the right
Both aircraft shall alter course to the left
The smaller aircraft shall give way to the larger aircraft
The aircraft with the other on its right shall give way

bank.question: An aircraft that is taking off must give way to an aircraft that is landing or on final approach
bank.explanation: According to Rule 11 of the Rules of the Air, aircraft on the ground or in the air must give way to aircraft that are landing or in the final stages of an approach to land

bank.question: What is the meaning of a series of green flashes from Aerodrome Control to an aircraft on the ground?
bank.explanation: A series of green flashes directed at an aircraft on the ground is the signal for the pilot to proceed with taxiing
options: Return to the starting point on the aerodrome

bank.question: In the UK Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) system, what does the colour mauve indicate?
bank.explanation: A mauve AIC covers subjects involving United Kingdom Air Traffic Control, such as airspace changes or communications procedures
options: Air Traffic Services and operational matters

bank.question: In Class G airspace, what is the distance from cloud requirement for a pilot flying a fixed-wing aircraft at 140 knots or less at 2,500ft AMSL?
bank.explanation: To maintain VFR in Class G airspace at or below 3,000ft AMSL and at 140kt or less, the pilot must remain clear of clouds and in sight of the surface
options: Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
Clear of cloud and 500ft vertically from cloud

bank.question: In the UK, a series of green flashes from the ground to an aircraft in flight means 'Cleared to land'
bank.explanation: A series of green flashes directed at an aircraft in flight means 'Return for landing', usually followed by a steady green for permission to land. 'Cleared to land' is indicated by a steady green light

bank.question: What is the meaning of a steady red light directed by Aerodrome Control to an aircraft in the air?
bank.explanation: A steady red light directed at an aircraft in flight signifies that the aircraft is not clear to land and must give way to other aircraft
options: The aerodrome is unsafe, do not land
Immediate distress, land as soon as possible
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Return for landing and wait for a green light

bank.question: Who is responsible for ensuring the aircraft is loaded within its weight and balance limits and that all required equipment is on board?
bank.explanation: The PIC is legally required to verify that the aircraft is safely loaded within its weight and balance limits and that all equipment for the flight is present
options: The aircraft owner or the operator
The Chief Flying Instructor of the flight school
The licensed engineer who signed the last maintenance release

bank.question: Under UK regulations, what is the maximum number of passengers allowed for a cost-sharing flight in a light aircraft?
bank.explanation: A PPL holder may not fly for remuneration, but may share 'direct costs' (fuel, fees, etc.) with up to 5 passengers, provided no profit is made

bank.question: A PPL holder may act as Pilot in Command (PIC) without a valid medical certificate, provided they are not carrying passengers
bank.explanation: ICAO Annex 1 specifically mandates that the holder of a pilot licence shall not exercise the privileges of that licence unless they hold a current medical assessment appropriate to the licence

bank.question: According to the '500-foot rule', what is the minimum distance an aircraft must maintain from any person, vessel, vehicle or structure?
bank.explanation: SERA 3105 specifies that except for take-off or landing, aircraft must not fly below 500ft from any person, vessel, vehicle or structure

bank.question: In Class C airspace, is a pilot required to obtain an Air Traffic Control (ATC) clearance before entering while flying under Visual Flight Rules (VFR)?
bank.explanation: Class C airspace is controlled; therefore, an ATC clearance must be obtained before entry, regardless of whether the flight is VFR or IFR
options: No, as long as the pilot maintains VMC at all times
Yes, a formal ATC clearance is mandatory for VFR flights in Class C
No, but the pilot must provide a 'notification of intent' to enter
Only if the pilot intends to land at an airport within that airspace

bank.question: What is the name of the report a pilot should file if they believe the safety of their aircraft was endangered by the proximity of another aircraft?
bank.explanation: An AIRPROX report should be filed whenever a pilot or controller considers that the distance between aircraft was such that the safety of the aircraft was compromised

bank.question: To operate under VFR at night, the cloud ceiling must be at least 1,500 feet
bank.explanation: The Serco/Standardised European Rules of the Air (SERA) and UK Law state that VFR flight at night requires a minimum cloud ceiling of 1,500 ft

bank.question: In Class E airspace, between which types of flights does Air Traffic Control provide separation for aircraft flying under VFR?
bank.explanation: While ATC provides information on IFR flights to VFR flights in Class E, they do not provide separation for VFR flights from any other traffic
options: No separation is provided to VFR flights
All flights from terrain and obstacles

bank.question: What does a steady red light from an aerodrome signal lamp indicate to an aircraft in the air?
bank.explanation: A steady red light directed at an aircraft in flight signifies that the pilot should give way to other aircraft and continue circling
options: Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Land immediately as the aerodrome is about to close
Aerodrome is unsafe, do not land
Return to the circuit and wait for a green flash to land

bank.question: In the event of an aircraft accident in the UK, within what time period must the pilot-in-command notify the Civil Aviation Authority?
bank.explanation: The Captain must notify the CAA without delay (within 72 hours) following a reportable accident or serious incident during flight operations

bank.question: The '500ft rule' does not apply to flight over the sea or sparsely populated areas
bank.explanation: The 500ft rule states that an aircraft shall not be flown closer than 500ft to any person, vessel, vehicle or structure, regardless of whether the area is congested

bank.question: When is it mandatory to file a flight plan for a VFR flight according to SERA?
bank.explanation: Under SERA, a flight plan is mandatory for any flight crossing an international border
options: Only if the flight is IFR
Only if the flight enters Controlled Airspace
Only if the flight is over 50 nautical miles
For any flight intended to cross an international border

bank.question: What are the VMC minima for distance from cloud for a VFR flight in Class G airspace at an altitude of 4,000ft AMSL?
bank.explanation: Standard VFR minima in Class G airspace above 3,000ft mean sea level include a horizontal distance from cloud of 1,500m and a vertical distance of 1,000ft
options: Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface

bank.question: To revalidate a Single Engine Piston (SEP) rating by experience, how many hours of flight time must be completed in the 12 months preceding the expiry date?
bank.explanation: To keep a PPL valid, a pilot must have completed 12 hours of flight time in the relevant class in the 12 months preceding the rating expiry

bank.question: The transponder code 7500 is used to indicate that an aircraft is subject to unlawful interference
bank.explanation: Transponder code 7500 is the internationally recognised code for an aircraft being subjected to unlawful interference (hijacking)

bank.question: What does a black letter 'C' on a yellow background indicate at an aerodrome?
bank.explanation: A black letter 'C' on a vertical yellow background identifies the location of the Air Traffic Services Reporting Office (Control Tower/C-Office)
options: The Air Traffic Services reporting office

bank.question: What does a horizontal white dumb-bell shape in the signal square of an aerodrome indicate?
bank.explanation: A horizontal white dumb-bell in the signal square informs pilots that they must use only the taxiways and hard surfaces for ground movements, not the grass
options: Landing is prohibited at this aerodrome
Glider flying is currently in progress
Special care is required during approach and landing
Use only hard surfaces (runways and taxiways) for movements

bank.question: Which ICAO Annex covers the 'Rules of the Air'?
bank.explanation: Annex 2 of the Chicago Convention contains the international Standards and Recommended Practices regarding the Rules of the Air

bank.question: A horizontal white 'L' in the signals square indicates that the aerodrome is open to light aircraft only
bank.explanation: A horizontal white 'L' displayed in the signals square over a 'T' indicates that light aircraft are permitted to take off and land on a part of the aerodrome other than the main runway

bank.question: What are the specific visual requirements for a pilot operating under a Special VFR (SVFR) clearance within a Control Zone?
bank.explanation: A Special VFR clearance allows flight in a Control Zone when conditions are below VFR minima, but the pilot must remain clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
options: 1.5 Km and 1,000 feet clear of clouds
Clear of cloud and with the surface in sight
5 Km and 1,500 feet vertically from cloud
3 Km and 1,000 feet vertically from cloud

bank.question: By definition, an aircraft is considered to be overtaking another if it is approaching from the rear within an angle of less than how many degrees?
bank.explanation: According to SERA, an aircraft is 'overtaking' if it is approaching another from the rear on a line forming an angle of less than 70 degrees with the plane of symmetry

bank.question: What is the main difference between an 'Air Traffic Control Service' and an 'Air Traffic Advisory Service'?
bank.explanation: An Air Traffic Control Service is provided to prevent collisions, while an Advisory Service only provides information to assist in safe separation
options: An Air Traffic Control Service issues instructions; an Advisory Service issues suggestions/information
An Advisory Service is only provided in Class A airspace
An Air Traffic Control Service is only available to IFR flights
There is no difference; they are different names for the same service

bank.question: ICAO Annex 12 is the document that specifically deals with 'Search and Rescue'
bank.explanation: ICAO Annex 12 governs 'Search and Rescue' and outlines the procedures and requirements for contracting states to provide SAR services

bank.question: In which section of the UK Aeronautical Information Publication (AIP) would you find information regarding General Flight Planning and En-route procedures?
bank.explanation: The UK AIP is divided into three sections: General (GEN), En-route (ENR), and Aerodromes (AD). Flight Planning is part of ENR

bank.question: A Flight Plan is considered 'overdue' if the aircraft has not landed within how many minutes of its Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA)?
bank.explanation: SERA/The Rules of the Air state that if a landing is not made within 30 minutes of the Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA), the flight is considered overdue

bank.question: Who is responsible for the operation and safety of an aircraft, and the safety of all persons on board, during flight time?
bank.explanation: The Commander is legally responsible for the safety of the aircraft and all persons on board during flight time
options: The Air Traffic Controller on duty
The Chief Flying Instructor of the club

bank.question: The standard radius of an Aerodrome Traffic Zone (ATZ) is always 5 nautical miles from the centre of the aerodrome
bank.explanation: An ATZ generally extends from the surface up to 2,000ft above aerodrome level (AAL) and usually has a radius of 2nm or 2.5nm depending on runway length

bank.question: What is indicated by a signal consisting of yellow crosses displayed on a taxiway?
bank.explanation: A line of yellow crosses indicates that the taxiway or part of the taxiway is unfit for aircraft movement
options: A taxiway is unfit for the movement of aircraft
Pilots should exercise caution due to grass cutting
The area is reserved for helicopter movements only

bank.question: What does a red square with a single yellow diagonal stripe displayed in a signal square mean?
bank.explanation: A red square with a single yellow diagonal indicates that the aerodrome is in a state of 'caution' and that the state of the landing area is poor
options: The aerodrome is closed to light aircraft
The state of the landing area is poor and caution is required
Gliders are being launched by winch

bank.question: What is the minimum flight visibility required for a VFR flight at night in the UK?
bank.explanation: SERA specifies that the standard 'VFR at night' visibility requirement is 5 km

bank.question: In Class D airspace, VFR flights are not separated from other VFR flights by Air Traffic Control
bank.explanation: In Class D airspace, ATC provides separation between IFR and IFR flights, and provides traffic information (and traffic avoidance advice on request) to VFR flights

bank.question: What does a signal consisting of a white double cross displayed in the signal square represent?
bank.explanation: A double white cross in the signal square indicates that the aerodrome is being used by gliders and such flights are in progress
options: The runway is blocked by a disabled aircraft
The aerodrome is closed for all fixed-wing traffic

bank.question: What is the requirement for a pilot regarding a change in medical fitness (e.g., a significant illness or injury)?
bank.explanation: A Pilot in Command must inform the CAA immediately if they develop any medical condition that is likely to interfere with the safe exercise of their licence privileges
options: Wait until the next scheduled medical examination
Only if the illness lasts longer than 90 days
Only if the pilot is over the age of 40
Inform the CAA in writing as soon as possible if the illness may affect flight safety

bank.question: To exercise the privileges of a PPL(A), what requirement must be met regarding the pilot's medical certificate?
bank.explanation: The medical certificate for a PPL must be valid at the time the privileges of the license are exercised. Periodical re-examination is required
options: The medical certificate must be valid
The medical certificate must have been issued within the last 5 years regardless of age
No medical is required if flying solo
The pilot must have their NHS records available for inspection

bank.question: The Certificate of Airworthiness must be carried on board the aircraft for every flight, including local circuits
bank.explanation: Documents such as the Certificate of Airworthiness and the Aircraft Radio Licence must be carried on international flights, but for domestic UK flights, they can often be left on the ground

bank.question: Except when necessary for taking off or landing, what is the minimum height an aircraft may fly over an organized open-air assembly of more than 1,000 persons?
bank.explanation: Rule 11 of the Rules of the Air states that an aircraft shall not fly over any assembly of 1,000 persons or more below 1,000ft

bank.question: What is the term used for the lowest forecast QNH for a designated altimeter setting region?
bank.explanation: In the UK, the Altimeter Setting Region (ASR) pressure setting is commonly referred to by the radiotelephony designator 'Regional QNH'

bank.question: Which transponder code should be selected to indicate a total loss of radio communication?
bank.explanation: Squawking 7600 is the international standard for notifying ATC of a radio communication failure

bank.question: Statement: What does a steady red light directed at an aircraft in flight signify - Do not land; give way to other aircraft and continue circling.
bank.explanation: A steady red light from the Control Tower directed at an aircraft in flight means the aircraft is not clear to land and must continue circling

bank.question: In the UK, what colour is an Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) containing administrative or advisory information?
bank.explanation: AIC Yellow contains information of an administrative nature or concerns safety through education. Air Law/Safety is White; Technical is Pink

bank.question: Under the '500-foot rule', what is the minimum distance an aircraft must maintain from any person, vessel, vehicle, or structure?
bank.explanation: Except for taking off or landing, aircraft must not fly closer than 500ft to any person, vessel, vehicle, or structure

bank.question: Which ICAO Annex is primarily concerned with Security and safeguarding civil aviation against acts of unlawful interference?
bank.explanation: ICAO Annex 17 focuses specifically on the protection of civil aviation against acts of unlawful interference

bank.question: Statement: Which of the following documents must be carried on board a UK-registered aircraft for an international flight - The manufacturer's original design blueprints.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The Certificate of Airworthiness. UK aircraft must carry several documents, including the Certificate of Airworthiness, the Registration, and the Radio Licence

bank.question: While on the ground, what does a flashing green light from Aerodrome Control indicate to a pilot?
bank.explanation: A flashing green light to an aircraft on the ground means the aircraft is cleared to taxi
options: Return to starting point on aerodrome
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling

bank.question: Which ICAO Annex contains the international standards for Security and safeguarding aviation against acts of unlawful interference?
bank.explanation: ICAO Annex 17 specifically deals with the protection of international civil aviation against acts of unlawful interference

bank.question: In Class G airspace, what is the minimum flight visibility for a VFR flight operating at 2,500ft AMSL at a speed of 160 knots?
bank.explanation: Under SERA, the minimum visibility for VFR flight below 3,000ft AMSL in Class G airspace (outside a congested area) is 5km if the speed is above 140kt

bank.question: Statement: What is the minimum distance an aircraft must maintain from any person, vessel, vehicle or structure, according to the SERA/Standardised European Rules of the Air, except for take-off and landing - 500 feet.
bank.explanation: Rule 5 (Landings and take-offs near persons or vessels) states an aircraft shall not fly closer than 500 feet to any person, vessel, vehicle or structure, except when landing or taking off in accordance with normal aviation practice

bank.question: When two aircraft are approaching head-on at approximately the same altitude, what action is required?
bank.explanation: According to SERA, when two aircraft are approaching head-on, or approximately so, both must alter their course to the right
options: The lighter aircraft must give way
Each aircraft shall alter its heading to the right

bank.question: In the UK Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) system, what does the colour RED signify?
bank.explanation: UK AICs are issued in five colours: White (Administrative), Red (Safety), Yellow (Operational), Mauve (Legal), and Green (Environmental)

bank.question: What are the required colours for the navigation lights on the wingtips of a flying aircraft at night?
bank.explanation: At night, an aircraft must display a steady red light on the left (port) side and a steady green light on the right (starboard) side
options: Green on the left, Red on the right
Red on the left, Green on the right
White on the left, Red on the right
Red on the left, White on the right

bank.question: Statement: The UK Aeronautical Information Publication (AIP) is divided into which three main sections - GEN, COM, MET.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: GEN, ENR, AD stories. GEN (General) covers administrative and legal info; ENR (En-Route) covers airspace; AD (Aerodromes) covers specific details of airports

bank.question: In the UK Aeronautical Information Service, what colour is used for an Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) that relates to Safety?
bank.explanation: The pink AIC series contains information regarding safety-related topics and operational matters

bank.question: In Class G airspace, who is responsible for the separation of a VFR flight from other aircraft?
bank.explanation: In Class G (uncontrolled) airspace, the pilot is primarily responsible for maintaining their own separation from other aircraft
options: ATC provides separation from all other traffic
The pilot is responsible for maintaining separation from other aircraft
ATC provides separation only from IFR traffic
The pilot is only responsible for separation from other VFR traffic

bank.question: What does a steady red light from a signal gun indicate to an aircraft in flight?
bank.explanation: A steady red light directed at an aircraft in flight means the pilot must give way to other aircraft and continue circling
options: The aerodrome is unsafe, do not land
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Return for landing followed by a steady green light

bank.question: Statement: For a Special VFR flight in a Control Zone, what is the minimum required cloud ceiling - 600 feet.
bank.explanation: Special VFR allows flight within a Control Zone (CTR) in conditions below VMC, provided the cloud ceiling is at least 600ft

bank.question: The UK Aeronautical Information Publication (AIP) is divided into which three main sections?
bank.explanation: GEN (General) covers administrative and legal info; ENR (En-Route) covers airspace; AD (Aerodromes) covers specific details of airports
